tells: 1. The laugh barely builds: across the 1 s strip only the woman in white (hand to mouth) and the green-hoodie man (lean) change; the purple-top and short-blonde women at the right table stay on the same clasped-hands pose with the same face, so the room reads as two people reacting rather than a crowd (club-5-strip.png, right table and centre table, all six frames)

2. Resting poses repeat: almost every seated front-row figure has forearms on the table with hands clasped round the candle, the same posture copied table to table (club-6-held.png and club-1-wide.png, front row centre to right)

3. The back of the house is flat black standing cut-outs with no seated bodies, tables or motion, layered like cardboard behind a seated front row; nobody in it is alive (club-1-wide.png and club-2-mid.png, upper half behind row 1)

4. Close face is game-character, not person: waxy uniform skin, glassy eyes with no wet highlight, a lip shape that reads as a speaking viseme rather than a smile, and a faint dark edge halo round the shoulders against the blurred background (club-4-face.png, face centre and collar/shoulder outline right)

5. Same avatars visibly reused across tables and venues (green hoodie, purple top, short-blonde woman, magenta track top are the same people in every venue), which breaks the 'real room' read once noticed (club-1-wide.png front row; compare theatre-1-wide.png and openmic)

1. Front row sits like a police line-up: square to camera, upright, knees apart, hands on knees or clasped between them, evenly spaced; and row 2 sits so high it looks like people standing behind the seats (theatre-1-wide.png, rows 1-2 centre)

2. Duplicate avatars side by side: the short-blonde woman in grey appears twice in row 2 and again in the held frame, and blonde bun / hoodie figures repeat within a few seats (theatre-1-wide.png, row 2 left at ~300,380 and right at ~930,370; theatre-6-held.png left foreground and centre)

3. Faces in rows 2-3 are flat and self-lit like pasted masks, with no shading from the stage spill and no eye detail, so they read as dolls (theatre-2-mid.png, man upper-left ~170,250 and row 2 faces; theatre-3-mid.png row 2)

4. Low-LOD bodies show: pale, untextured cylinder arms and stiff shoulders on the near-left woman, and bright white chest panels on dark silhouettes in the upper-left rows (theatre-6-held.png, left foreground woman's arm and upper-left rows ~380,330)

5. The close face expression is ambiguous (eyes cast down off-stage, mouth open with lower teeth, brows level), so it reads as distaste or speaking rather than the start of a laugh; skin is waxy (theatre-4-face.png, centre)

1. The wide is a row of the same pose: nearly everyone in the front row leans forward with both hands on the knees, like a waiting room, and the second row is a solid wall of heads (openmic-1-wide.png, front row centre to right)

2. Bodies collide in the held frame: the capped man in the blue jacket bows his head down onto his neighbour, and the hoodie woman leans into the green-shirt woman with arms and knees crossing through each other (openmic-6-held.png, ~330,420 and ~700-760,450-600)

3. Disengaged posing: the hoodie woman in the front row hangs her head to her lap while everyone else watches the stage, which reads as asleep rather than listening (openmic-3-mid.png, centre ~700,420)

4. Close face edges: stripy, dithered alpha on the hair at the right temple, and a dark halo round the jacket and shoulder against the blurred background; eyes slightly unfocused, expression neutral (openmic-4-face.png, hair right ~800,250 and shoulder/left edge)

5. The laugh in the strip is social and good (the green-shirt woman turns to her friend, who leans in), but only that pair and the afro man move; the yellow-shirt man and the denim-jacket man keep the same face for the whole second (openmic-5-strip.png, left half of every frame)
